'''Adana''' was a celestial body located in the [[Adana system/Legends|Adana system]] of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Faust/Legends|Faust]] researcher [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Nuvo Vindi/Legends|Nuvo Vindi]].<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Adana was first mentioned in "[[Tanith: the Guest-Star Wars]]," a [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] adventure written by [[Olivier Frot]] and published in the [[March]] [[1990]] [[Graal 24|twenty-fourth issue]] of the French-language magazine [[Graal (magazine)|''Graal'']] for use with [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. In the adventure, by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], Adana is claimed by official records to be the homeworld of the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Tanith Seyze]], who no longer had a family and consequently joined the Alliance. In actuality, Seyze was neither Human nor from Adana, instead being a vampiric entity that [[Diet/Legends|fed]] on the psychic energy of her victims.<ref name="Graal24">{{GraalCite|24|Tanith: the Guest-Star Wars}}</ref> The adventure is considered [[Canon|noncanonical]] with respect to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity.<ref name="Unlicensed">{{UnlicensedStatus}}</ref>

The first canonical mention of Adana in the Legends continuity was in the [[2010]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'' by [[Jason Fry]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> The [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Adana [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the celestial body, in grid square L-10.<ref name="EAOC" />
